milestones.title: A modern beginning
milestones.text: Athens hosts the first modern Olympic Games. The gold, silver and bronze labels used here are retrospective for the earliest editions.

milestones.title: Women join the Games
milestones.text: Paris becomes the first modern Olympic edition to include women. Early programmes also feature sports such as croquet, cricket and basque pelota.

milestones.title: Three absent editions
milestones.text: The world wars cancel three Summer Games. Their gaps remain visible in the timeline.

milestones.title: Two cities, two continents
milestones.text: Melbourne stages the Games, while equestrian events take place in Stockholm because of Australian quarantine rules.

milestones.title: South Africa returns
milestones.text: Barcelona marks South Africa’s return after its exclusion during apartheid. Elana Meyer and Wayne Ferreira / Piet Norval win silver medals.

milestones.title: Back to Paris
milestones.text: A century after Paris 1924, the city hosts again. Breaking makes its Olympic debut; the programme includes 329 medal events.

notes: 30 held Summer Games, 1896–2024; 5,761 events with medal awards, across 51 sport / discipline labels. The 1916, 1940 and 1944 Games were cancelled. Tokyo 2020 was held in 2021. Future editions and the 1906 Intercalated Games are outside this archive.

17,825 event-level medal awards. A team, pair or relay counts once in a delegation’s table. Ties remain separate awards, including ties between competitors from the same delegation. Rankings sort by gold, silver, then bronze; exact ties share a rank. Athlete views count the named people in medal rosters, which can be incomplete, include alternates or retain name variants. They are not a certified individual medal register or a full participation record.

Art competitions, demonstration events, special prizes, Paralympics and Youth Games are excluded. Figure skating at London 1908 and Antwerp 1920, and ice hockey at Antwerp 1920, are included because they were part of those Summer editions. The 1908 cycling sprint and sailing classes without entrants remain as no-medal records. The disputed 1920 18-foot dinghy gold is excluded and explained on its event card. Los Angeles 1932’s unawarded team jumping event is absent from the medal archive.

Historical delegations stay separate, including Soviet Union, Unified Team, East Germany, West Germany, United Team of Germany, Russia, ROC and Individual Neutral Athletes. Czech Republic and Czechia share the display name Czechia. “Mixed” means an event category, not a multinational delegation; “Open” covers selected events without a men-only or women-only classification. Early category labels and programme definitions can differ by source.

method: Every medal event of every Summer Games, read from Wikipedia’s list of medal winners for that Games at the recorded revision: the event and its sport, the men’s, women’s, mixed or open category, and the gold, silver and bronze awards with the delegation and the athletes the list names. A team, pair or relay counts once in a delegation’s table; ties are separate awards; the medal table of every Games reconciles by delegation and colour against the cited comparison table. Art competitions, demonstration events and the 1906 Intercalated Games are outside the archive. Host cities are placed on the Natural Earth land silhouette at approximate coordinates.
